_note: Machine-checked catalog manifest + the SINGLE SOURCE for the shipped example library (REQ-CATALOG-CONFORMANCE / REQ-CATALOG-METADATA, ADR-0027/0028). Each `diagrams` row carries the full per-row schema {file,type,family,name,catalogId?,school,note,audience}; audience ∈ C(clinician)|L(client)|B(both); a client-facing (L/B) diagram has a sensible picture rendering. `conformance/catalog.test.ts` enforces the schema + catalog↔corpus fidelity; `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` GENERATES the catalog's example-library table from this file (drift-checked); the editor gallery derives its non-showcase items from it. `newTypes` are the catalogued ◇ shapes with no renderer yet.

diagrams.name: CBT 5-part (hot cross bun)
diagrams.note: A generic maintaining cycle. The model underpins evidenced CBT; the diagram itself is a co-drawn heuristic, not a measure.

diagrams.name: Vicious flower (depression)
diagrams.note: A low-mood maintaining cycle. A formulation, not an outcome measure; the way out is behavioural activation.

diagrams.name: Panic vicious cycle
diagrams.note: The fear-of-fear loop: sensation → catastrophic thought → panic → safety behaviour → more sensations. A well-evidenced cognitive model.

diagrams.name: Social-anxiety cycle
diagrams.note: Self-focused attention + safety behaviours maintain the fear. A well-evidenced model; the cycle is the formulation.

diagrams.name: OCD maintenance cycle
diagrams.note: Intrusion → appraisal → distress → compulsion → relief → more intrusions. Underpins evidenced ERP; the exit is response prevention.

diagrams.name: Nervous-system state ladder / window of tolerance
diagrams.note: Bands of nervous-system states + what shifts between them, and a way back. A useful map; over-physiologised versions inherit the contested polyvagal theory — use as metaphor.

diagrams.name: CAT SDR — reciprocal roles + trap
diagrams.note: Reciprocal roles, traps/dilemmas/snags and exits. CAT works *through the alliance*; the map is a co-drawn heuristic — its one dismantling trial found the reformulation letter redundant.

diagrams.name: IFS parts map
diagrams.note: Self + protective/wounded parts. IFS is popular but thinly evidenced (~2 RCTs); "parts" is a metaphor — avoid reifying it, especially with dissociation.

diagrams.name: Parts map — perfectionism
diagrams.note: A worked parts map with a contested-origin marker where schools disagree about a part — a formulation, not a measure.

diagrams.name: Schema mode map
diagrams.note: Modes + Healthy Adult "in the driver’s seat". Among the better-evidenced models here (RCTs for personality disorder).

diagrams.name: Karpman drama triangle
diagrams.note: Persecutor/Rescuer/Victim role-switching. A widely-taught heuristic; "Victim" means a *stance*, not an actual victim of harm — never use it to dismiss real harm.

diagrams.name: Genogram (3-generation)
diagrams.note: Three-generation family map. Widely used but weakly evidenced as an instrument (SAGE-PAGE found no clinical effect); privacy/family-reading caveats.

diagrams.name: Relational field
diagrams.note: People and ties in the person’s world. A practice tool, not a validated instrument.

diagrams.name: Resource / anchor map
diagrams.note: Strengths, safe people/places, values — the "path of hope". Co-created.

diagrams.name: Body / sensation map
diagrams.note: Where emotions are felt in the body. The descriptive maps replicate cross-culturally; body-mapping-as-treatment is thinner; can be triggering for trauma.

diagrams.name: Life timeline / lifeline
diagrams.note: Events and turning points over time. A narrative organiser, not a measure.

diagrams.name: Longitudinal CBT formulation
diagrams.note: How early experiences → beliefs → rules → current triggers. Belief links are tentative hypotheses — the least-reliable part of any formulation.

diagrams.name: 5 Ps timeline
diagrams.note: Predisposing/precipitating/perpetuating/protective factors. By nature a grid, not really a diagram; shown here as a factor timeline. (Not coined by Macneil 2012.)

diagrams.name: Malan two triangles
diagrams.note: Conflict (defence/anxiety/feeling) + Person (therapist/other/parent). The therapy is moderately evidenced; the diagram itself is untested as a mechanism.

diagrams.name: Intervention sequence
diagrams.note: Ordered steps/skills toward a goal. A plan, not a measure.

diagrams.name: DBT chain analysis
diagrams.note: Vulnerability → prompt → links → behaviour, with a skill to interrupt it. DBT is strongly evidenced; do it with kindness, not blame.

diagrams.name: ACT Choice Point
diagrams.note: A moment’s fork: toward-moves vs away-moves, with hooks and values. ACT is evidenced; the format is a delivery tool.

diagrams.name: Crisis / safety plan
diagrams.note: One decision per step, resources on every screen, no dead-ends. A collaborative plan — never a no-suicide contract or a risk-prediction tool.

diagrams.name: Relapse-prevention plan
diagrams.note: Triggers → early signs → coping → support. The approach is evidenced; the worksheet isn’t. A wellness plan, NOT a crisis plan.

diagrams.name: Goal ladder / scaling
diagrams.note: Small steps toward a preferred future. A practice tool.

diagrams.name: Ritual structure (van Gennep)
diagrams.note: Van Gennep phases with a secular variant. Rituals reliably affect *subjective* anxiety/meaning, not objective disease markers (§F).

diagrams.name: Stages of Change wheel (TTM)
diagrams.note: The change cycle. Popular but genuinely contested as a *stage* model (West 2005) — treat the stages as a heuristic.

diagrams.name: Safety-behaviour maintenance cycle
diagrams.note: Threat belief → anxiety → safety behaviour → disconfirmation blocked → the belief survives. Mechanism shown experimentally; the safety-behaviour vs adaptive-coping line is contested (Telch).

diagrams.name: Reciprocal-roles diagram (CAT)
diagrams.note: criticising ⇄ criticised, and the procedure that follows from the role. The core CAT construct; co-created and owned by the client.

diagrams.name: Dilemma — a false either/or (CAT)
diagrams.note: A false either/or ("comply or be rejected") that traps. A school-agnostic loop shape; the way out is naming the false binary and finding a third option.

diagrams.name: Snag — success undone (CAT)
diagrams.note: Legitimate goals undone by guilt ("I don't deserve it" / others will lose out). A self-sabotage pattern; the way out is allowing the good thing and tolerating the guilt.

diagrams.name: SORC functional analysis
diagrams.note: Stimulus → Organism → Response → Consequence — a shared map of one episode and where to intervene. An influential clinician heuristic, hard to standardise.

diagrams.name: ABC(DE) functional analysis
diagrams.note: Activating event → Beliefs → Consequence, then Dispute → Effect. A teaching / self-monitoring tool; belief-mediation is the REBT differentiator.

diagrams.name: Trauma timeline (titrated)
diagrams.note: Events + meanings + resources across time, paced. Distress caveat — consent, resourcing and grounding first; titrate exposure.

diagrams.name: Health-anxiety loop (disorder-specific)
diagrams.note: Body sensation → "something is wrong" → checking / reassurance → more noticing. A maintaining cycle; the way out is dropping the safety behaviour and tolerating uncertainty.

diagrams.name: PTSD maintenance — Ehlers–Clark (disorder-specific)
diagrams.note: A sense of current threat kept alive by intrusions + avoidance / suppression / hypervigilance. Underpins evidenced trauma-focused CBT; pace the work and resource first.

diagrams.name: Metacognitive CAS — Wells (disorder-specific)
diagrams.note: Worry / rumination + threat-monitoring + thought-control (the Cognitive-Attentional Syndrome) maintain distress. The way out is detached mindfulness, not more thinking.

diagrams.name: Eating disorder — transdiagnostic, Fairburn (disorder-specific)
diagrams.note: Over-evaluation of shape / weight / control → strict dieting → binge → compensation → confirms the over-evaluation. Underpins evidenced CBT-E; the diagram is the formulation, not the measure.

diagrams.name: Psychosis — cognitive maintenance, Morrison (disorder-specific)
diagrams.note: An unusual experience → a threatening interpretation → distress + safety behaviours → the meaning goes unchallenged. A shared, non-judgemental account of experience.

diagrams.name: Empowerment (winner's) triangle
diagrams.note: The hopeful reframe of the drama triangle: Creator / Challenger / Coach. A heuristic, not an outcome measure — the counterpart to Karpman.

diagrams.name: Structural dissociation (ANP/EP)
diagrams.note: An Apparently-Normal Part that runs daily life, dissociated by a barrier from trauma-fixed Emotional Parts. Influential in complex trauma; supporting neuroimaging is small-n — a high-stakes map, pace it.

diagrams.name: Ecomap — person in their systems
diagrams.note: The person / family and their external systems — supports and strains, by tie quality. A widely used practice tool, not a validated measure.

diagrams.name: Social atom / sociogram
diagrams.note: Significant others mapped by closeness and tie quality (close / distant / fused / cut-off). A practice tool for the relational field.

diagrams.name: Externalising map — narrative (disorder-agnostic)
diagrams.note: The person is never the problem — "the Worry" is mapped as a separate entity, alongside unique outcomes and allies who know the real person. A co-authored, client-led tool.

diagrams.name: Cultural genogram — heritage & identity
diagrams.note: Family plus heritage, faith, identity and migration. An assessment aid — hold it with cultural humility; the client is the expert on their own culture.

diagrams.name: Exposure / fear ladder
diagrams.note: Feared situations ranked by SUDS, climbed least → most. Exposure therapy is strongly evidenced; the ladder is a planning aid — the inhibitory-learning turn questions strict graded ordering / SUDS-drop stopping rules.

diagrams.name: CFT three circles (threat / drive / soothing)
diagrams.note: Three emotion-regulation systems sized by balance — grow the soothing system. CFT has systematic-review support for self-criticism/shame; "three systems" is a neuroscientific simplification, not a brain map.

diagrams.name: DBT states of mind
diagrams.note: Reasonable ∩ Emotion = Wise Mind. Core DBT psychoeducation — a heuristic (not a brain model) inside an evidenced programme.

diagrams.name: Values bullseye
diagrams.note: Life domains plotted as on-/off-target to chosen values; the spread of darts shows where to close the gap. A client values-clarification reflection — a teaching aid, not a measure of a good life.

diagrams.name: Tree of Life
diagrams.note: A strengths-forward life portrait by botanical zone — roots (origins), ground (present), trunk (skills/values), branches (hopes), leaves (people), fruits (gifts). A widely-used, culturally-adaptable, client-led practice tool — co-created, not an assessment.
